items.title: Why Analysts Expect Nearly 7% More Than Take-Two Does
items.summary: Our latest piece, Could A GTA VI That Meets Guidance Hurt Take-Two Stock?, started from an odd quarter: fiscal second-quarter net bookings of $1.6 billion came in below the company's own $1.62 billion to $1.67 billion range, yet the shares rose 8.3% the next day. That piece left a question open: why do analysts expect more revenue this year than Take-Two Interactive Software (TTWO) says it will deliver.

items.title: GTA VI Comes Out Thursday. She Bought 588 Take-Two Shares the Day GTA V Launched. They’re Worth $131,994
items.summary: A grandmother who bought 588 Take-Two shares at $17.00 on Grand Theft Auto V's launch day in 2013 holds $131,994 as GTA VI arrives Nov. 19. She can sell 187 shares at a 0% federal rate, sell everything for about $12,465 in tax, or give shares to her grandson.
